user: How do I add a vendor?
answer:
To add a vendor, go to Niural Pay > Vendors > Add vendor (or + Add new vendor from inside the Add bill form).

Fill in:
1) General information: Vendor type (Individual or Business), Vendor country, Vendor name (legal registered name), Entity, Department.
2) Contact information: Contact number, Email address.
3) Tax & compliance: EIN and upload a Tax document (required if you’ll generate 1099s).
4) Vendor agreement: Upload contract (PDF/DOC/DOCX).
5) KYB verification: If you’ve run the check, tick “Mark this vendor as KYB verified.”
6) Home or business address and Mailing address.
7) Click Create vendor.

Tip: You can also start from the Add bill flow and choose + Add new vendor, then continue.
sources: Part 2 — Niural Pay > How to add a vendor

user: What does KYB status mean for a vendor?
answer: KYB status refers to Know-Your-Business verification for a vendor. It can be either Verified or Not verified. It’s separate from whether the vendor is Active, and having a Not verified status is a common reason a payment cannot proceed.

user: A bill says Ready for payment but I can't find a transaction for it. Why?
answer: A bill can show Ready for payment even if no transaction has been created yet. Transactions are the money that actually moved, and that record is separate from the bill’s status. If you don’t see a matching transaction, it hasn’t been generated yet or the payment hasn’t moved to a transaction yet. You can verify transactions in the Transactions history (Created at, Payment method, Status, Amount). If a bill is Ready for payment but no transaction exists, you’ll see the bill waiting for the payment to move to a transaction.

user: How do I create an invoice for a customer?
answer:
Here’s how to create a customer invoice:

1) Go to Niural Pay → Invoices → Create invoice.
2) Fill in Customer name and Invoice title.
3) Link a Contract if one exists; otherwise the invoice will show as Unlinked.
4) Enter Entity and department.
5) Add Invoice details: Reference number, Currency, Invoice code, Invoice date, Payment term (e.g. One Week), and Payment due.
6) At line level: Item, Quantity, Rate, Discount %, Tax rate, Amount.
7) Add any Notes and an Additional attachment if needed.
8) Check Subtotal, Additional discount %, Tax amount and Net amount.
9) Answer whether this is a recurring invoice. If Yes, it will be scheduled and visible under Schedules.
10) Click Create invoice.

Important: Creating an invoice does not send it automatically. It sits as Email not sent until you send it to the customer.
sources: Part 2 — Niural Pay > How to create a customer invoice

user: Why does a bill show two currencies?

user: Why can't I pay an employee who just joined?
answer: They can’t be paid yet because the new hire is still in Onboarding. A hire only becomes payable after every onboarding step is complete, and the step that often prevents payment is Form I-9 Section 2. Section 2 must be completed within 3 business days of the employee’s first day of work, and the dashboard shows a Form I-9 tracker for outstanding items. To get paid, finish all onboarding steps (including Form I-9 Section 2) and then you can process payroll.

user: and for a bill instead?
answer:
To add a bill in Niural Pay:

1) Go to Niural Pay → Bills → Add bill. A template selector sits next to the title.
2) You can use the Upload vendor invoice panel on the right: drop in the vendor’s document (JPEG, PNG or PDF, up to 10MB) and Niural extracts vendor, amount, dates and other details automatically. Then check the fields rather than typing them.
3) To fill manually:
   - Choose the vendor you want to pay, or + Add new vendor.
   - Pick the Contract to bill against to enable anomaly checks.
   - Entity and department.
   - Invoice details: Invoice number, Invoice date, Invoice currency, Due date.
   - Line items: Item, Quantity, Rate, Tax %, Discount %, Amount. Add more items as needed; totals calculate as you go.
   - Add Notes (up to 500 characters) and any Additional attachments.
4) Click Next: Review details, check the summary, and confirm.

The bill then appears with its own Invoice ID alongside the vendor’s number. If an approval policy applies it lands under Needs approval; otherwise it moves toward Ready for payment. Paying is a separate step—open the bill and use Pay invoice.
